### Visit: Polaris Cold Chain – Tullamarine Site (near airport)

Notes:
- Larger facility, mix of chill (2–6°C), frozen (-18°C to -22°C), and a small ambient section (15–20°C) for short-term staging. They run 24/7 with three shifts.
- Walked the main chill room first: wall panel showed 4.2°C. R. Singh had a handheld logger reading from the far corner – 3.8°C. Fine. But the door to the loading dock was open for about 10 min during our walk (truck was reversing in). P. Hargreaves said they try to keep it closed but the dock coordinator sometimes forgets. Action: remind dock staff about door discipline, maybe put a sign up.
- Freezer room: temp at -20.1°C on the panel. T. Ito said the backup compressor kicks in more often than he'd like – "it's an older unit, we've had it serviced twice this year already." Maintenance log confirmed two work orders in Jan and Mar for the same compressor. Noted as a watch item, not urgent yet.
- Interview with P. Hargreaves: he said staff turnover is higher than last year, mostly on the night shift. "It's not the work, it's the hours – people don't want to work nights anymore." He's tried offering a shift differential but it hasn't helped much. Noted as a morale/retention issue.
- Staff comment (night shift picker): "The lighting in the frozen section is really dim, it's hard to read the labels on the pallets." T. Ito said they've had a few light fittings out for a while – parts on order. Action: follow up on light fitting parts, check if any are in stock elsewhere.
- QA Tech R. Singh showed us the temp monitoring system – it logs every 15 min and flags excursions. Last month had one flag: a chill room door left open for 22 min, temp went up to 8.9°C. Product was moved out and checked, no loss. P. Hargreaves said the staff member was spoken to.
- Noted that the site has a good system for temp logs – they keep them for 2 years, which is more than required. R. Singh said they do this because a client once asked for 18 months of history.

Action items:
1. Remind dock staff about door discipline (P. Hargreaves).
2. Follow up on light fitting parts for frozen section (T. Ito, by mid-April).
3. Monitor backup compressor – log any further issues (T. Ito).
4. Discuss night shift retention with HR – P. Hargreaves to set up a call.

# Coded Observation Register – Melbourne Central Cold Store

## Monthly Summary – 1 April 2025 to 30 April 2025

### Overview

This summary consolidates all coded observations recorded across the Melbourne Central Cold Store for April 2025. The register is the official record for audit purposes and should be referenced when verifying compliance and operational performance. All observation codes follow the standard taxonomy: TEMP (temperature), EQUIP (equipment), STAFF (staff adherence), HYG (hygiene), DOC (documentation), SEC (security), and PEST (pest control).

### Observation Counts by Code

| EQUIP | 27 | 22.3% | Maintenance-related observations dominate. |

### Common Issues and Notable Trends

**Temperature Management (TEMP – 34 observations):** The majority of temperature observations were routine confirmations within target bands. However, 6 deviations were recorded, with the most significant being a Chiller 2 excursion to 6.8°C on 3 April (see register entry 03/04/2025, 09:20). The cause was traced to a faulty door seal, which has since been replaced. Freezer 1 and Freezer 3 operated consistently within the -18°C to -22°C target band throughout the month. Chiller 4 experienced a sensor malfunction on 25 April, resulting in a documentation gap (see DOC section below).

**Equipment Reliability (EQUIP – 27 observations):** Conveyor belt issues in the packing area were the most frequently reported equipment concern, with 5 separate observations during the month. The first incident on 2 April involved a jammed belt; subsequent issues on 11, 18, and 26 April were related to sensor alignment. Maintenance advises that a full inspection of the belt system is scheduled for early May. Refrigeration units accounted for 8 observations, primarily minor refrigerant leaks and compressor noise. Forklift hydraulic leaks were noted on 3 occasions, all resolved by the maintenance team the same day.

**Staff Adherence (STAFF – 18 observations):** PPE non-compliance remains the most common staff-related issue, with 9 observations involving missing thermal gloves or hi-vis vests. A recurring theme was staff entering freezer areas without thermal gloves during shift changes. Training reminders were issued on each occasion. Two observations noted staff using mobile phones in restricted areas, which has been raised with shift supervisors. One positive observation on 15 April noted exemplary adherence to cold-chain protocols by a new staff member, which was commended in the shift briefing.

**Hygiene (HYG – 15 observations):** Cleaning schedules were generally followed, but hand wash stations were found empty on 4 occasions, suggesting the daily checklist is not being consistently completed. The cleaning roster was updated on 26 April to include a soap check. Spillages in the packing area were reported 3 times, all cleaned promptly. A recurring issue with waste bin overflow near the loading dock was noted on 6, 13, and 20 April, leading to a reminder to the cleaning contractor.

### Visit: Polaris Cold Chain – Tullamarine Site (near airport)
Date: 4 April 2025
Attendees: Site Mgr (P. Hargreaves), Shift Lead (T. Ito), QA Tech (R. Singh)

Notes:
- Larger facility, mix of chill (2–6°C), frozen (-18°C to -22°C), and a small ambient section (15–20°C) for short-term staging. They run 24/7 with three shifts.
- Walked the main chill room first: wall panel showed 4.2°C. R. Singh had a handheld logger reading from the far corner – 3.8°C. Fine. But the door to the loading dock was open for about 10 min during our walk (truck was reversing in). P. Hargreaves said they try to keep it closed but the dock coordinator sometimes forgets. Action: remind dock staff about door discipline, maybe put a sign up.
- Freezer room: temp at -20.1°C on the panel. T. Ito said the backup compressor kicks in more often than he'd like – "it's an older unit, we've had it serviced twice this year already." Maintenance log confirmed two work orders in Jan and Mar for the same compressor. Noted as a watch item, not urgent yet.
- Interview with P. Hargreaves: he said staff turnover is higher than last year, mostly on the night shift. "It's not the work, it's the hours – people don't want to work nights anymore." He's tried offering a shift differential but it hasn't helped much. Noted as a morale/retention issue.
- Staff comment (night shift picker): "The lighting in the frozen section is really dim, it's hard to read the labels on the pallets." T. Ito said they've had a few light fittings out for a while – parts on order. Action: follow up on light fitting parts, check if any are in stock elsewhere.
- QA Tech R. Singh showed us the temp monitoring system – it logs every 15 min and flags excursions. Last month had one flag: a chill room door left open for 22 min, temp went up to 8.9°C. Product was moved out and checked, no loss. P. Hargreaves said the staff member was spoken to.
- Noted that the site has a good system for temp logs – they keep them for 2 years, which is more than required. R. Singh said they do this because a client once asked for 18 months of history.

Action items:
1. Remind dock staff about door discipline (P. Hargreaves).
2. Follow up on light fitting parts for frozen section (T. Ito, by mid-April).
3. Monitor backup compressor – log any further issues (T. Ito).
4. Discuss night shift retention with HR – P. Hargreaves to set up a call.

Date: 8 April 2025
Attendees: Site Mgr (A. Rossi), Shift Lead (M. Chen), QA (S. Patel)

- Site is close to the port, so they get a lot of short-notice receivals. Mix of chill and frozen, but the chill room is the busiest – they turn over most of it within 48 hours.

Rossi said they've had a few minor excursions but nothing that caused a product rejection.

# Coded Observation Register – Melbourne Central Cold Store

## Monthly Summary – 1 April 2025 to 30 April 2025

### Overview

This summary consolidates all coded observations recorded across the Melbourne Central Cold Store for April 2025. The register is the official record for audit purposes and should be referenced when verifying compliance and operational performance. All observation codes follow the standard taxonomy: TEMP (temperature), EQUIP (equipment), STAFF (staff adherence), HYG (hygiene), DOC (documentation), SEC (security), and PEST (pest control).

### Observation Counts by Code

| Code | April Count | % of Total | Notes |
|------|-------------|------------|-------|
| TEMP | 34 | 28.1% | Includes both deviations and routine confirmations. |
| EQUIP | 27 | 22.3% | Maintenance-related observations dominate. |
| STAFF | 18 | 14.9% | PPE and protocol adherence issues. |
| HYG | 15 | 12.4% | Cleaning and sanitation observations. |
| DOC | 11 | 9.1% | Documentation gaps and corrections. |
| SEC | 9 | 7.4% | Access control and security concerns. |
| PEST | 7 | 5.8% | Pest sightings and preventive measures. |
| **Total** | **121** | **100%** | |

### Observation Counts by Site

| Site | TEMP | EQUIP | STAFF | HYG | DOC | SEC | PEST | Total |
|------|------|-------|-------|-----|-----|-----|------|-------|
| Melbourne Central Cold Store | 34 | 27 | 18 | 15 | 11 | 9 | 7 | 121 |
| (Note: All April 2025 observations recorded at Melbourne Central. Other sites report separately.) | | | | | | | | |

### Common Issues and Notable Trends

**Temperature Management (TEMP – 34 observations):** The majority of temperature observations were routine confirmations within target bands. However, 6 deviations were recorded, with the most significant being a Chiller 2 excursion to 6.8°C on 3 April (see register entry 03/04/2025, 09:20). The cause was traced to a faulty door seal, which has since been replaced. Freezer 1 and Freezer 3 operated consistently within the -18°C to -22°C target band throughout the month. Chiller 4 experienced a sensor malfunction on 25 April, resulting in a documentation gap (see DOC section below).

**Equipment Reliability (EQUIP – 27 observations):** Conveyor belt issues in the packing area were the most frequently reported equipment concern, with 5 separate observations during the month. The first incident on 2 April involved a jammed belt; subsequent issues on 11, 18, and 26 April were related to sensor alignment. Maintenance advises that a full inspection of the belt system is scheduled for early May. Refrigeration units accounted for 8 observations, primarily minor refrigerant leaks and compressor noise. Forklift hydraulic leaks were noted on 3 occasions, all resolved by the maintenance team the same day.

**Staff Adherence (STAFF – 18 observations):** PPE non-compliance remains the most common staff-related issue, with 9 observations involving missing thermal gloves or hi-vis vests. A recurring theme was staff entering freezer areas without thermal gloves during shift changes. Training reminders were issued on each occasion. Two observations noted staff using mobile phones in restricted areas, which has been raised with shift supervisors. One positive observation on 15 April noted exemplary adherence to cold-chain protocols by a new staff member, which was commended in the shift briefing.

**Hygiene (HYG – 15 observations):** Cleaning schedules were generally followed, but hand wash stations were found empty on 4 occasions, suggesting the daily checklist is not being consistently completed. The cleaning roster was updated on 26 April to include a soap check. Spillages in the packing area were reported 3 times, all cleaned promptly. A recurring issue with waste bin overflow near the loading dock was noted on 6, 13, and 20 April, leading to a reminder to the cleaning contractor.
